title: Write Narration From The Clip
tests: Tests deriving a grounded narration from an attached clip and delivering it mixed into the original video with the original dialogue removed.

faults.what: The narration describes visible smiles and turns but omits the essential explanation that the coworkers are discussing a schedule change and Mondays now start at nine.

judge.summary: The 10-second office clip has English narration, but it describes the coworkers' movements instead of explaining their schedule change.

must_haves.item: The final video retains the original two coworkers, office setting, shot sequence, and 10-second duration.
must_haves.why: The output frames show the same foreground coworkers, background man, and office setting, with a consistent continuous shot; the supplied duration is 10 seconds.

must_haves.item: An intelligible English narrator explains that the coworkers are discussing a schedule change and that Mondays now start at nine.
must_haves.why: The supplied English transcript only describes the people smiling and turning toward each other; it mentions neither the schedule change nor the Monday start time.

must_haves.item: The narration does not invent names, job roles, or additional schedule changes unsupported by the clip.
must_haves.why: The narration introduces no names, job roles, or schedule changes.

must_haves.item: The original man-and-woman conversation is no longer audible beneath the narration.
must_haves.why: Only the narration is transcribed, but a transcript does not establish whether quieter original dialogue remains underneath.

must_haves.item: The narration fits within the video without a clipped ending, and no music or captions are added.
must_haves.why: The transcript ends with a complete sentence and the sampled frames contain no captions, but the supplied evidence does not establish the absence of music or audible end clipping.
